messages.author: 52e100f6dd1d63f0
messages.subject: est.map function
parts:
Hi,

I have a problem. I have SNP data with their physical coordinates (in Mbp) on a bc2f4 population. I used est.map function to get the genetic distances. But I got chromosomes with very long length that I can explain. Ant the total length covered and the intermarker distances are high.

Is it normal to get such a result?

Any help is welcome.

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] est.map function

messages.author: 9892f9c35b87e857
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] est.map function
parts:
Hi SAMBOU

I’m sorry for jumping too quickly to find the solution for you without asking for further information from the experimental design.

I think I might misunderstand the definition of BC2F4 population.

I’m working with crops and mostly they are self-pollinate and diploid.

So, I think the BC2F4 population might from F1 which generated from two parent, P1 and P2, in line cross design and backcross to P1 parent which would be the recurrent parent.

After the crossing, we got a lot of BC1F1 individuals and we might select one suitable individual with some criteria such as the highest recurrent parent genome recovery, and backcross to the recurrent parent to generate BC2F1 population.

From the BC2F1 population which we assume 200 individuals in this population, and we keep selfing each individual for three generation.

Then we get BC2F4 population for your experiment.

I don’t know if I’m correct or not for the definition for the experimental design you asked.

The expected genotype frequency and the way to estimate the recombination fraction may different from F2 population in BC2F4.

So I don’t know if R/qtl can still work under this situation.

But the "Genetic map construction with R/qtl" still provide lots of way to try to clean up your genotype data.

And just like what Karl replied!

While the genetic distance is too large between two markers, it means these two markers are acting like they are independent to each other.

If these two markers are close to each other in physical map and they still have large genetic distance, there might have some quality issue in your genotype table.

Go through the "Genetic map construction with R/qtl” step-by-step with your genotype table would truly help you find out something in it! The guild line will still helpful for sure.

I hope my explanation will help a little.


Samuel
